# Module II: Eddy Dissipation Concept

## Filtered Species Transport Equation {.filtered-species-slide}

::: {.filtered-species-layout}

::: {.filtered-species-equation}
$$
\frac{\partial\bar{\rho}\widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}}{\partial t}
+
\frac{\partial\!\left(\bar{\rho}\widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}\widetilde{u}_{i}\right)}{\partial x_i}
=
\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}
\left(
\left[\rho D_{\alpha}+\frac{\mu_t}{\mathrm{Sc}_t}\right]
\frac{\partial\widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}}{\partial x_i}
\right)
+
{\color{red}\overline{\dot{m}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime\prime}}}
$$
:::

::: {.filtered-species-field-label}
Filtered field:
:::

::: {.filtered-species-definition}
$$
\overline{\phi(\mathbf{x},t)}
\equiv
\int G(\mathbf{r};\Delta)\,\phi(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{r},t)\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}
$$
:::

::: {.filtered-species-closure}
In LES, the filtered chemical source term\
is *unclosed*.
:::

::: {.filtered-species-kernel}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tophat-kernel.svg){fig-alt="Top-hat spatial filter kernel, equal to one for distances within half the filter width and zero elsewhere."}
:::

:::

## Turbulent Batch Reactor Model {.tbr-slide}

::: {.tbr-layout}

::: {.tbr-subtitle}
FDS flavor of EDC
:::

::: {.tbr-true-field}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-true-mass-fraction.png){fig-alt="True mass-fraction field with continuous turbulent mixing."}
:::

::: {.tbr-idealized-field}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-idealized-mass-fraction.png){fig-alt="Idealized mass-fraction field with three discrete composition levels."}
:::

::: {.tbr-true-label}
True
:::

::: {.tbr-idealized-label}
Idealized
:::

::: {.tbr-scale-label}
Mass Fraction
:::

::: {.tbr-scale}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-mass-fraction-scale.png){fig-alt="Grayscale mass-fraction scale from zero, black, to one, white."}
:::

::: {.tbr-unmixed-label}
$\zeta$: Unmixed fraction
:::

::: {.tbr-equation}
$$
\overline{\dot{m}_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime\prime}}
= \rho \Biggl[
{\color{#70ad47}\underbrace{
  {\color{black}\frac{{\color{#5b9bd5}\zeta}}{\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}}
  \left(\widehat{Y}_{\alpha}-\widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}^{0}\right)}
}_{\text{Mixing}}}
+
{\color{red}\underbrace{
  {\color{black}\left(1-{\color{#5b9bd5}\zeta}\right)
  \frac{\mathrm{d}\widehat{Y}_{\alpha}}{\mathrm{d}t}}
}_{\text{Reaction}}}
\Biggr]
$$
:::

:::

## The Unmixed Fraction {.unmixed-fraction-slide}

::: {.tbr-layout}

::: {.tbr-true-field}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-true-mass-fraction.png){fig-alt="True mass-fraction field with continuous turbulent mixing."}
:::

::: {.tbr-idealized-field}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-idealized-mass-fraction.png){fig-alt="Idealized mass-fraction field with three discrete composition levels."}
:::

::: {.tbr-true-label}
True
:::

::: {.tbr-idealized-label}
Idealized
:::

::: {.tbr-scale-label}
Mass Fraction
:::

::: {.tbr-scale}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/tbr-mass-fraction-scale.png){fig-alt="Grayscale mass-fraction scale from zero, black, to one, white."}
:::

::: {.unmixed-fraction-equation}
$$
\begin{array}{c@{\;}c@{\;}c@{\;}c@{\;}c@{\;}c@{\;}c}
\widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}(t)
& =
& {\color{blue}\zeta(t)}
& \widetilde{Y}_{\alpha}^{0}
& +
& {\color{red}\left(1-\zeta(t)\right)}
& \widehat{Y}_{\alpha}(t)
\\[0.45em]
\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\alpha}{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\mathrm{tot}}
&
& {\color{blue}\underbrace{
  \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}U}{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\mathrm{tot}}
}_{\substack{\text{Unmixed}\\\text{fraction}}}}
& \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\alpha}{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}U}
&
& {\color{red}\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}M}{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\mathrm{tot}}}
& \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}\alpha}{\mathrm{kg}\text{-}M}
\end{array}
$$
:::

:::

## Evolution of the Unmixed Fraction {.unmixed-evolution-slide}

::: {.unmixed-evolution-layout}

::: {.unmixed-evolution-rate}
$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}\zeta}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\frac{\zeta}{\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}}
$$
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-solution}
$$
\zeta(t) = \zeta_0\,\mathrm{e}^{-t/\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}}
$$
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-plot}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/unmixed-fraction-decay.svg){fig-alt="Exponential decay of the unmixed fraction from one toward zero over ten mixing times."}
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-y-label}
$\zeta(t)$
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-x-label}
$t/\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}$
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-initial}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/unmixed-evolution-initial.png){fig-alt="Initially segregated turbulent mass-fraction field with strong light and dark variations."}
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-arrow-first aria-hidden="true"}
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-intermediate}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/unmixed-evolution-intermediate.png){fig-alt="Partially mixed field with reduced mass-fraction variations."}
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-arrow-second aria-hidden="true"}
:::

::: {.unmixed-evolution-mixed}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/unmixed-evolution-mixed.png){fig-alt="Fully mixed field with uniform mass fraction."}
:::

:::

## Mixing Time Scale {.mixing-scale-slide}

::: {.mixing-scale-layout}

::: {.mixing-scale-selection}
$$
\tau_{\mathrm{mix}} = \max\Bigl(\tau_{\mathrm{chem}},
\min\bigl(\tau_d,\tau_u,\tau_g,\tau_{\mathrm{flame}}\bigr)\Bigr)
$$
:::

:::: {.mixing-scale-plot}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/mixing-time-scale-curves.png){fig-alt="Log-log plot of mixing time versus grid size, bounded by chemical and flame time scales, with diffusion, turbulent, and gravitational scaling regimes."}

::: {.mixing-scale-eta}
$\Delta = \mathrm{O}(\eta)$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-d-scaling}
$\tau_d \sim \Delta^2$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-u-scaling}
$\tau_u \sim \Delta^{2/3}$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-g-scaling}
$\tau_g \sim \Delta^{1/2}$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-flame-label}
$\tau_{\mathrm{flame}}$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-chem-label}
$\tau_{\mathrm{chem}}$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-x-label}
$\Delta\ (\mathrm{m})$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-y-label}
$\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}\ (\mathrm{s})$
:::

::::

::: {.mixing-scale-diffusion}
$$
\tau_d = \frac{\Delta^2}{D_{\mathrm{F}}}
$$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-turbulence}
$$
\tau_u = \frac{C_u\Delta}{u'}
= \frac{C_u\Delta}{\sqrt{(2/3)\,k_{\mathrm{sgs}}}}
$$
:::

::: {.mixing-scale-gravity}
$$
\tau_g = \sqrt{2\Delta/g}
$$
:::

:::

## Exercise: Kolmogorov Scaling {.kolmogorov-slide}

::: {.kolmogorov-layout}

::: {.kolmogorov-prompt}
Use a model inertial range energy spectrum to derive the scaling law.
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-scaling}
$$
\tau_u \sim \Delta^{2/3}
$$
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-spectrum-intro}
The inertial range spectrum is
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-spectrum-equation}
$$
E(k) = C_K\,\varepsilon^{2/3}\,k^{-5/3}
$$
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-constant}
$C_K = 1.5$\
Kolmogorov constant
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-dissipation}
$\varepsilon$\
KE dissipation rate
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-wavenumber}
$k$\
Wavenumber
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-portrait}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/andrey-kolmogorov.png){fig-alt="Andrey Nikolaevich Kolmogorov at a blackboard."}
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-caption}
Andrey Nikolaevich Kolmogorov\
(1903–1987)
:::

:::: {.kolmogorov-plot}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/kolmogorov-energy-spectrum.png){fig-alt="Model energy spectrum with an inertial-range power-law decay and a vertical dashed line marking the grid Nyquist limit."}

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-guides}
![](figs/eddy_dissipation_concept/kolmogorov-spectrum-guides.svg){fig-alt=""}
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-slope}
$-5/3$
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-cutoff}
$k = \dfrac{\pi}{\Delta}$
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-nyquist}
grid Nyquist limit
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-x-label}
$k$
:::

::: {.kolmogorov-plot-y-label}
$E(k)$
:::

::::

:::
